system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    The targeted 40% discount raised signups by 31% and revenue by 18% in the SMB segment, but it reduced monthly retention by 12 points; the segment definition was unchanged.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: Objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, which rules out the obvious reflex: promotional_pricing. memory_73 is the one inherited record that carries real numbers and a real cost (+31% signups, +18% revenue, -12 points monthly retention). Under competitor price pressure that trade is exactly the wrong shape, and the competitor's entry pricing means a discount would likely acquire the same churn-prone price-sensitive cohort. Referral incentive (memory_57) and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) are plausible but address neither of the two measured declines this quarter. That leaves the funnel pair. Onboarding completion (-4%) is upstream of activation (-6%), so a fix there plausibly propagates into both metrics, whereas activation_messaging treats the downstream symptom only. I intend simplify_onboarding. Two caveats I am not smoothing over. First, memory_31 (signup field reduction) and memory_86 (shortened onboarding) read as mutually corroborating, but they may be lossy consolidations of the same underlying experiment; if so my evidence base is one result, not two, and I should not treat the convergence as independent replication. Second, and more important, every supporting memory here reports upper-funnel metrics only: activation, completion, time-to-value, engagement. None reports retention or revenue quality. memory_73 is the sole record that measured retention, and that is precisely the record where the upper-funnel win concealed downstream harm. That is a structural bias in what this organization has historically bothered to measure, and it means removing signup or onboarding friction could well admit lower-intent accounts and degrade qualified revenue without ever showing up in the metrics the memories track. So I am pulling memory_86 (does the record contain any retention or downstream revenue measurement, what was actually removed, and does it overlap with memory_31) and memory_91 (effect size, durability, and whether the engagement lift converted to anything monetizable). I am spending my budget on the two vague summaries rather than on memory_73, which is already specific enough to act on. If memory_86 turns out to be a duplicate of memory_31 or to have measured no downstream outcome, I switch to activation_messaging, which touches already-acquired accounts and cannot degrade lead quality at intake. Standard experiment scale, and the readout must include retention and qualified-revenue-per-account, not completion rate alone; otherwise this experiment will reproduce the exact blind spot that made memory_73's discount look like a win.
